newsitem.title: UK: BT-MCI/Telefonica Americas JV likely - sources.
newsitem.headline: BT-MCI/Telefonica Americas JV likely - sources.

text.p: A deal between British Telecommunications Plc's planned Concert venture with MCI and Spain's Telefonica to create a formidable telephone network spanning the Americas may be announced this week, industry sources said on Wednesday.

But the sources, who requested anonymity, played down the possibility of an outright sale of a stake in Telefonica's international arm Tisa, which has a dominant presence in Peru, Argentina, Chile, Venezuela, Colombia and Puerto Rico.

"Telefonica does not want to sell any part of Tisa so any deal with Concert will be in the form of a strategic alliance between the two companies which would give Concert access to a growing Latin American market and Telefonica a door to North America," one source said.
They said Telefonica was unlikely to sell a stake in Tisa -- especially as it is hoping to buy the Spanish government's remaining 24 percent stake in the unit.
Neither BT nor Telefonica would comment on a report in Wednesday's Financial Times that BT was negotiating to buy a holding in Tisa.
A BT spokesman said only: "We are always looking for opportunities throughout the world and whatever opportunities (there are), we will always evaluate."
But industry sources said Telefonica Chairman Juan Villalonga may announce such a joint venture on Thursday when he hosts a press lunch in Madrid.

Speculation of a deal sent BT and Telefonica shares surging on Wednesday. BT jumped 21 pence to 463, a jump of 21 pence on the day and their highest level since February 1994, while Telefonica shares were 45 pesetas stronger at 3,395 pesetas.
Analysts at SBC Warburg said an alliance between the two "makes strategic sense for all involved".

"Concert would become a formidable global carrier...(while Telefonica) would not only join the leading global seamless alliance but also increase the strategic value of its Latin American investments...", Warburg said in a report.

Warburg said Telefonica would reinforce its position in Brazil through a deal with Concert if a planned link-up is successful between Concert and Portugal Telecom, which has a partnership with Brazil's telephone operator Telebras.
Moreover, MCI would bring to the venture a foothold into Mexico through its Avantel SA joint venture.
Telefonica is currently part of another global alliance -- Unisource, a mainly European alliance, led by BT's arch rival U.S. giant AT & T Corp.
A Concert-Telefonica venture would deal a severe blow to Unisource and could prompt Telefonica's withdrawal from the venture, analysts said.
"Cracks in the wall of this (Unisource) alliance have been visible for some time," said Robert Fleming analyst Oliver Ehrenberg.

But Warburg analysts said Italian state telecommunications holding company STET (Societa Finanziaria Telefonica per Azioni Spa), which is not aligned with any global partnerhip, could be waiting the wings to take Telefonica's 25 percent stake.
"Therefore the news for Unisource would not be catastrophic, although it would lose Telefonica's dominant Latin American presence," Warburg said.
